newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve EU-Palestinian accord amid crisis.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve EU-Palestinian accord amid crisis.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Wednesday a trade and aid deal between the European Union and the Palestinian Authorities amid fears the crisis in the Middle East peace process would undermine the agreement.

The Dutch president of the EU Council of Ministers, Michael Patijn, attacked Israel for going ahead with the construction of new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem, in the face of fierce protests from the Palestinians and the international community.
"The (EU) Council regards the settlement policy as at odds with international law," Patijn told the European Parliament.

"Moreover the Israeli settlement policy preempts the negotiations on the eventual status of the area. The peace process and the confidence of the Palestinians and Arab countries is being undermined by this," the minister continued.
Patijn said the EU was doing its best, through its aid to the Palestinian Authorities, to improve the economic conditions of the Palestinians in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.
He hinted that Israel's decision earlier this week again to prevent Palestinians entering Israel to work threatened to undermine these efforts and further damage the search for peace.

"The Palestinian economy is in a parlous state. A lengthy closure of the border with Israel is not acceptable. That would lead to further decline in the standard of living of Palestinians in the Palestinian areas and would be more likely to create a bridgehead for unrest and violence," Patijn said.
He warned the Palestine Authorities that the EU held them responsible too for curbing the recent upsurge in violence and getting the peace process back on the rails.

Manuel Marin, EU commissioner for the Mediterranean, told Euro-MPs the EU had been put under intense pressure not to conclude the new trade and aid agreement with the Palestinians, which he said was of great political significance.

Marin said it was in the interest of the United States to let the EU, which was making intensive diplomatic efforts to get Israelis and Palestinians back to the negotiating table, play an equally prominent role in any future Middle East peace talks.

The new agreement will run until 1999 -- the period set out in the Middle East peace accord for the transition of the Occupied Territories to autonomous Palestinian rule -- when the two sides will begin talks on an even more comprehensive pact.
